title: Nutrient Crew: Different Jobs, One Body

zones.label: Carbohydrates
zones.summary: Carbohydrates are the body’s first source of quick, usable energy.
facts: The brain and active muscles rely heavily on glucose from carbohydrates.
Whole grains, fruits, vegetables, rice, oats, and pasta are familiar sources.
Fiber-rich carbohydrate foods also support digestion and lasting fullness.

zones.label: Protein
zones.summary: Protein supplies building blocks for growth and repair.
facts: Amino acids help build new cells and repair tissue.
Beans, lentils, eggs, fish, poultry, nuts, dairy, and alternatives can provide protein.
Protein is construction material as well as a nutrient—not the body’s first quick fuel.

zones.label: Fats
zones.summary: Fats provide long-lasting energy, protection, warmth, and vitamin absorption.
facts: The body needs fat; it is not a nutrient to eliminate.
Nuts, seeds, avocado, oils, and fatty fish provide useful fats.
Balance and variety matter more than labeling one food good or bad.

zones.label: Vitamins and Minerals
zones.summary: Micronutrients are needed in small amounts for many specialized body jobs.
facts: Calcium supports bones and teeth; iron helps blood carry oxygen.
Different vitamins support healing, immunity, eyes, skin, and more.
Variety across fruits, vegetables, grains, dairy, and alternatives helps cover needs.

zones.label: Water
zones.summary: Water supports nearly every body system.
facts: It helps regulate temperature and transport nutrients.
Water cushions joints and helps remove waste.
Regular drinking is especially useful before and after active play.

quiz.question: Which department is the first source of quick usable energy?
Which department supplies building blocks for growth and repair?
Which department supports long-lasting energy, protection, and vitamin absorption?
Which department includes calcium and iron for specialized jobs?
Which department cools, transports, cushions, and helps remove waste?
